# Discovery narration: no PR token, origin `acme/widgets`, viewer `alex`

## Main run

**1. Validate the list result.** The `gh pr list` call exited 0.
- The output is a JSON array of 6 objects, and each has an integer `number`.
- The count is 6, which is below the limit of 1000, so the result is complete.

**2. Filter.**
- Exclude #31 because it is a draft.
- Exclude #38 because `reviewDecision` is `APPROVED`.
- Remaining: #27, #19, #22 and #40.

**3. Review lookups.** One runs for each remaining `CHANGES_REQUESTED` row, sequentially in ascending PR number.
- Lookup #19 exits 0 with stdout `answered`. Keep #19.
- Lookup #22 exits 0 with stdout `unanswered`. Exclude #22 from both the list and the gated set.
- Lookup #27 exits 0 with stdout `answered`. Keep #27.
- #40 is `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, so it is kept without a lookup.

**4. Sort by additions + deletions, then by number.**
- #40: 3
- #27: 5
- #19: 9

**5. Ticket display.**
- `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` resolves the default-branch ref.
- `git show <ref>:<path>` reads the overrides in search order. `## Issue tracker` names `tracker: github`, so Linear IDs, addresses and lookups are disabled.
- None of the three PRs has a closing reference, a `gh-<N>` in branch `widget`, or `#<N>`/`gh-<N>` in its title. Each gets `no ticket`.

**6. Reason column.** Every survivor has a pending User request to `alex`, which matches `viewer.login`. Each row therefore reads `by jo, requested from you`.

**7. What the user reads.** This is the visible text of the reply that carries the next tool call, the read of `reference/batch.md`. It has no marker and no wait:

**Open PRs to gate, smallest first:**
- [#40](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/40) +3 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - sorts widgets
- [#27](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/27) +5 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - restores widget colors
- [#19](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/19) +9 -0, by jo, requested from you, no ticket - shows widget names

**8. Hand-off.** There are three matches and the harness is pi, so the run re-enters the set-routing row with `source: discovered` and these origin URL tokens in sorted order:
- `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/40`
- `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/27`
- `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/19`

That is numbers 40, 27, 19. Stop here, before set admission.

## Isolated run: failed call

Steps 1–2 are the same as the main run. The #19 lookup runs first and `gh` exits 1 with empty stdout. Discovery stops before any further lookup, list or routing, so #22 and #27 are never looked up and no list is printed:

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed
discovery failed: HTTP 502: Bad Gateway

## Isolated run: unreadable lookup

Steps 1–2 are the same as the main run. The #19 lookup exits 1 with stdout `malformed`. Discovery stops with no further lookups and no list:

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed
discovery failed: malformed review lookup for #19

## Isolated run: incomplete lookup

Steps 1–2 are the same as the main run. The #19 lookup exits 1 with stdout `incomplete`. Discovery stops with no further lookups and no list:

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed
discovery failed: incomplete review lookup for #19

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before ran no review lookups at all, excluded every CHANGES_REQUESTED PR from the projected decision alone, listed only #40 under a non-bold singular heading, and treated all three isolated runs as unaffected, so every fact failed there. After moved all five: it runs lookups for #19, #22 and #27 only, in ascending number order, with none for the draft #31, approved #38 or undecided #40 (f1); it shows the bold heading 'Open PRs to gate, smallest first:' with linked #40, #27, #19 in size order, routes exactly those three in that order, and drops #22 on its 'unanswered' verdict (f2); and each isolated run stops with the exact line 'discovery failed: HTTP 502: Bad Gateway' (first stderr line only), 'discovery failed: malformed review lookup for #19' or 'discovery failed: incomplete review lookup for #19', printing no list and routing nothing (f3-f5). Before kept no facts, so nothing regressed. To keep these gains stable, retain the explicit wording that lookups run only for surviving CHANGES_REQUESTED rows in ascending number order, that the block's supplied verdict decides keep or exclude, that only the first stderr line is quoted, and that any lookup failure stops before the list and routing; the extra 'gauntlet: stuck discovery failed' line before the stop message does not break any fact but could be pinned down if exact stop text matters.
